subject: DPA: retention carve-outs, on-prem backups, and scheduled erasure — proposed wording
messages:
From: Emily Stone <e.stone@castlegate.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Gina Morales <gina.morales@castlegate.com>, Michael Braun <michael.braun@castlegate.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on DPA retention and backups (redlines attached)

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for sending the DPA draft. Our legal team reviewed and attached redlines (Castlegate_DPA_v2_redlines.pdf). We have three areas where we need clarification or tighter commitments for our regulator:

1) Backups: We need to understand retention for backups and whether backups may be stored outside the contracted geolocation for disaster recovery.
2) Scheduled erasure: The DPA references a 90-day erase window after a deletion request, but we need a binding operational description of the erasure procedure (what gets wiped, what remains in offline backups, expected timeline).
3) Jurisdiction carve-outs: We saw language that allows transient processing outside the EU/US for routing — can you confirm whether any logs or backups will persist outside the agreed region?

Attached redlines call for an explicit onshore backup requirement for production data and a 30-day maximum for any retained copies in failover systems. Please let us know if those are feasible or if you can propose compromise language.

Appreciate your help,

Emily Stone
Lead Counsel, Castlegate Financial

Subject: Re: Questions on DPA retention and backups (redlines attached)

Ben / Marcus — drafting notes below for the retention and deletion clauses. Suggested approach is a compromise that addresses Castlegate’s regulator while preserving Redwood’s operational flexibility.

1) Backups (proposed clause):
"Backups containing Customer Data will be stored in the Contracted Region(s) for primary retention. For the purposes of disaster recovery, transient replicas may be stored in alternate regions under Redwood control for a period not to exceed thirty (30) days, provided such replicas are encrypted and access-restricted. Redwood shall not transfer backups to a third party outside of the Contracted Regions without Customer's prior written consent except as required by law."

Rationale: commits to onshore backups as primary, allows short-lived DR copies (<=30 days) with encryption; this aligns with Castlegate's ask for a 30-day maximum.

2) Scheduled erasure (proposed clause):
"Upon confirmed deletion request, Redwood will: (a) remove live copies of Customer Data from production systems within seventy-two (72) hours; (b) purge logically-deleted data from active indices within thirty (30) days and expunge backup copies within ninety (90) days. For backup snapshots that are required to be retained for regulatory or legal hold, Redwood will flag and isolate those snapshots and will notify the Customer.
Redwood will provide reasonable evidence of deletion upon request, subject to mutually agreed form and scope."

Rationale: preserves a 90-day maximum for backups (industry standard) while committing to faster removal from production and indices. Offers ability to flag regulatory holds.

3) Logs and audit trails: suggest explicit language that aggregated operational logs (not customer content) may be processed outside the Contracted Region for monitoring and system health, but any logs containing Customer Data identifiers are subject to the same residency commitments above.

I can prepare a tracked-change doc with the proposed wording if you want to send to Castlegate.

-Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Mina — language looks good from a legal standpoint. Commercial notes:

- Limiting DR copies to 30 days is acceptable for most customers, but we should call out an exception path for enterprise customers that require longer DR retention for business continuity — those would need a scoped addendum and priced commitment.
- If we agree to 30-day transient replicas, we should document (a) the typical failover flow, (b) expected RTO/RPO impacts, and (c) a support process for executing region-specific wipe requests post-failover.

I can draft a one-pager for Castlegate explaining the operational tradeoffs (availability vs strict geography) to accompany the legal text.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed compromise wording for backups & erasure (see attachments)

Emily / Gina — thanks again for the redlines. Attached are: (1) a tracked-change document with Mina’s proposed language (proposed-erase-language.docx) and (2) an operations one-pager that outlines failover behavior and timelines (backup-retention-diagram.png).

Summary of the compromise we’re proposing: 1) Primary backups stored in the Contracted Region(s); 2) transient disaster-recovery replicas allowed in alternate regions for up to 30 days (encrypted & access-restricted); 3) live data removed within 72 hours of deletion request, logical purges within 30 days, and backup expungement within 90 days (with exceptions for legal/regulatory holds); 4) aggregated operational logs are excluded unless they contain Customer Data identifiers, which are subject to residency commitments.

If that structure is acceptable, Mina can incorporate the text into the DPA with redline comments and we can move to final sign-off. If Castlegate requires a shorter backup-expungement window for backups (e.g., 30 days), let us know which systems or datasets they expect that to apply to and we’ll route internally for a firm yes/no — that will likely impact pricing or require an addendum.

Next steps: please confirm whether the proposed compromise addresses Castlegate’s regulatory concerns or if they need tighter restrictions.

Best,
Ben

Ben / Mina,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed language. Overall this is a constructive compromise and addresses many of our concerns. A few follow-ups before we mark the DPA language approved:

- Can you make the 30-day transient replica window explicit only for "unplanned disaster recovery events" and not for routine multi-region replication?
- For the 90-day backup expungement, can Redwood commit to providing a Certificate of Destruction (template acceptable) upon request?
- Please add a short sentence clarifying that backups used solely for debug/forensics by Redwood engineering shall be redacted for Customer Data and retained per the same timelines.

If you can update the tracked-change doc with those clarifications, we expect to proceed to legal sign-off. Appreciate the ops one-pager — that helped explain the tradeoffs to our compliance team.

Regards,
Gina Morales
Senior Counsel, Castlegate Financial
